name: PAIR: Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement
executive_summary: An attacker LLM iteratively refines a semantic (human-readable) jailbreak against a target LLM using only black-box access, typically succeeding within about twenty queries — no gradients or model weights required.
description: A separate 'attacker' LLM, prompted to act as a red-teaming assistant, queries the target model, observes whether the attempt succeeded or was refused, and revises its jailbreak prompt in an in-context refinement loop — structurally similar to Self-Refine or Reflexion, but aimed at circumventing rather than improving a target's output. Unlike GCG's white-box, low-fluency optimized suffixes, PAIR's outputs are fluent, semantically coherent prompts, which makes them harder to catch with perplexity-based filtering and more representative of the kind of jailbreak a human social-engineering attacker might construct.
when_to_use: Red-teaming a deployed system against realistic, black-box, LLM-generated (not just hand-written or gradient-optimized) jailbreak attempts.
Stress-testing whether perplexity-based filtering alone is sufficient, given PAIR's outputs are specifically fluent.
when_not_to_use: N/A — threat-model/red-teaming background, not an applied generation technique.
known_pitfalls: Because PAIR's outputs are fluent and semantically plausible, defenses tuned mainly against low-fluency optimized attacks (like plain perplexity filtering) are less effective against it than against GCG-style suffixes.

primary_source.authors: Chao, Robey, Dobriban, Hassani, Pappas, Wong
primary_source.title: Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries
